Hi Sam / Alicia —

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. As we discussed, the February QBR will include: a 30‑40 minute executive product update (roadmap highlights relevant to BrightVerge), followed by a technical demo tailored to your integration team and a 20‑30 minute Q&A. Because your execs have a tight window, I wanted to surface two scheduling approaches and the operational tradeoffs so we can pick the least disruptive one: 

Option A — Compressed single session (75 minutes total)
- Exec update + demo in the same block.
- Pros: Single meeting on your calendar, simpler for execs.
- Cons: Harder to go deep on integration details; engineering may need to prioritize high‑level walkthroughs.

Option B — Split sessions (30 min exec update + 60 min deep demo on a separate day)
- Pros: Technical team gets an uninterrupted slot for walkthroughs and live staging.
- Cons: Requires one more calendar slot and coordination for recording/attendance.

Constraints from our side:
- Our product lead (Priyom) is on travel 2/10–2/12 and can only join remotely with limited morning availability.
- We need a recorded demo and permission to capture a short snippet of your API call logs for the performance slide (we'll redact tokens).
- If we compress to 75 minutes, we will likely cut the live run‑through of your custom pipeline; we can instead prepare a short recorded example.

Proposed windows (all PST):
- 2028-02-11 09:00–10:15 (Option A)
- 2028-02-11 14:00–15:30 (Option B — exec + deep demo same day, back‑to‑back)
- 2028-02-14 10:00–11:00 (deep demo only, if split)

Can you confirm which approach you prefer and any hard constraints on attendees? If you prefer Option B, please confirm a preferred date for the technical deep demo. I will coordinate with Priyom, Monica, and Rohan for runbook/ops coverage.

Attached: proposed-runbook-v1.pdf (ops fallback checklist) and qbr-draft-agenda.xlsx

Thanks,
Stephanie
